text.p: These are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- ELectoral Commission working in top gear. Voting documents for October 26 general election start being distributed tomorrow.
- Indiscriminate use of affidavits can "contaminate" course of justice, warns the president of the Chamber of Advocates at start of the judicial year.

- Election mail close to outstripping daily Christmas volume. Malta's political parties are increasingly using mailshots as the October 26 election approaches and post office workers are working overtime and on weekends to keep up.

- Labour leader Alfred Sant promises a boost for the self- employed and small businesses. He says a Labour government will remove VAT introduced by the government last year, replacing it with customs duties that were in place in 1994.

- Prime Minister Eddie Fenech Adami says ruling Nationalist Party, in office since 1987, promises host of services to the elderly to help them continue to live in their homes rather than in homes for elderly.
